Science Debate

Two first places, two questions without clean answers

Seoul Youth Science Fair · Debate contest · 2024–2025

I was a lead speaker for two consecutive years, on topics chosen for how badly they resist a simple answer. Most of the work is reading — primary sources in English, then a position, then the discipline of dropping an argument that turns out to be unsupported.

The first year the question was whether the Anthropocene should be declared a geological epoch at all. The second was whether AI can be trusted as an instrument of environmental policy. Neither topic rewards confidence; both reward evidence.

  • 20241st place — 42nd Seoul Youth Science Fair, debate contest · Anthropocene
  • 20251st place — 43rd Seoul Youth Science Fair, debate contest · AI and environmental solutions
  • ContributionWrote and revised both team outlines; presentation files archived

Robotics

Nine seasons of VEX IQ

Team member, build and drive · 2017–present

I started at seven, mostly because a robot does exactly what you tell it and nothing else. That turned out to be the fastest way to learn that most of my instructions were wrong.

At the 13th VEX Asia-Pacific Championship our team took the Build Award and second place in Robot Skills. The second one is a driving prize, which is the one I care about more — a notebook can be written the night before, but you cannot talk your way through a match.

  • 2019Build Award (VIQC) — 13th VEX Asia-Pacific Robotics Championship
  • 2019Robot Skills, 2nd place (VIQC) — same championship
  • CurrentlyStill competing; now focused on the engineering notebook and judging

Leadership & School

Class president, then vice president

Elected by classmates · 2024–2026

In 2025 I ran for class president and won. In 2026 I moved to vice president so a classmate could take the chair. Both years the job was the same in practice: mediating between thirty people and one schedule, and being the person who has to say no.

  • 2025Class President · Model Student Award (Service)
